issue.title: Leading @route stops the & dependency leading run, so '@cash &foo:bar Buy milk' captures literal text

task_type_fields.impact:
- The prerequisite is silently dropped and the task text is polluted with the literal `&note:id`. Nothing errors, and the Mac live preview shows no dependency spans.
- A new `*` reverse-dependency sigil that reuses this lexer would inherit the same bug.
task_type_fields.repro:
`bob capture-parse -f json -- '@cash &foo:bar Buy milk'` returns body `"&foo:bar Buy milk"`, mode `task`, and no dependency spans. `bob capture` would create a task whose text literally contains `&foo:bar`, with no prerequisite.

`&foo:bar @cash Buy milk` and `Buy milk @cash &foo:bar` both parse the dependency correctly.

`docs/capture.md` ("Adding prerequisites with '&'") says modifiers "sit at the leading or trailing marker positions of the parent line, interleaving with destination, schedule, priority, and clipboard markers in either order".

Root cause: in `extract_line_dependencies` (`src/native/capture_language/dependencies.rs`, the "Leading run (parent line only)" loop after :531), the leading run breaks at the first token that is not a modifier. Unlike the trailing run, it never skips the `is_trailing_transparent` shapes (`@…` destination, etc.), so a leading `@route` stops it.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching the * capture syntax: the docs promise & modifiers interleave with a leading @route in either order, but the lexer silently treats them as prose.
